newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU wary about Napoli sale prospects.
newsitem.headline: EU wary about Napoli sale prospects.

text.p: The European Commission is wary about the possibility that Italy's Banco di Napoli, which is being rescued by the Italian Treasury, may be sold to a state-controlled bank.
"We have new doubts...if Banco di Napoli is taken over by a state-owned bank," a European Union source told reporters on Wednesday.
The Commission was apparently concerned that Napoli may be overvalued by state-owned bidders which could be a disguised form of state aid.

The Commission is probing a proposal by the Italian Treasury to recapitalise Napoli by 2.0 trillion lire under EU rules which ban state subsidies to businesses unless accompanied by a strict restructuring plan which ensures its long-term viability.
The source said that the Italian govenment had informed the Commission's competition services that it had received three preliminary offers to buy the loss-making bank.

Those came from Mediocredito Centrale, Banco Nazionale de Lavoro -- which has teamed up with insurance company INA --, and a joint offer by three foreign banks. The first two offers are from state-controlled firms.
The Italian Treasury is expected to receive firm offers for Napoli by December 20, the EU source said. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
